correctness.rationale: The two roots and the sign interval follow from the single maximum of h(S)=S exp(-gamma S) and the strict parameter inequality. Positive coordinates persist locally by the exponential solution of each coordinate's scalar multiplicative equation. With Q=sum_i w_i w_(i-1), direct summation gives S'=exp(-gamma S)Q-dS and (log P)'=h(S)-nd. For n=3, S^2/3-Q is one sixth of the sum of squared pairwise differences; for n=4, Q=(w1+w3)(w2+w4), bounded by S^2/4. Thus the scalar comparison S'<=S(h(S)/n-d) and the equilibrium S_+ of the scalar RHS give S<=S_+, including initial equality. Up to any first time reaching S_-, P is nondecreasing, which excludes that time by S>=n P^(1/n)>S_-. This supplies the tangency/invariance step even on the non-strict upper face. S<=S_+ and P>=P0 give the stated individual lower bounds, compactness and continuation. By monotonicity or the invariance principle, a forward-invariant omega-limit orbit must have S=S_+ and equality in the Q bound. For n=3 this gives all coordinates equal. For n=4 it gives equal odd and even sums, whose difference has derivative -exp(-gamma S)uv when equal, where u=w1-w3 and v=w2-w4. Hence uv is identically zero along such an orbit. Substituting the equal sums and exp(-gamma S_+)S_+/4=d gives u'=-dv, v'=du, so the only orbit with uv identically zero is the origin in (u,v), proving convergence. The positive diagonal data strictly below the lower equilibrium decay to zero, showing optimality among the stated uniform product thresholds. Equality at the lower diagonal equilibrium cannot be added to the recovery criterion. For n>=5, substituting a small first Fourier mode into Q-S^2/n gives a strictly positive quadratic contribution proportional to cos(2pi/n), consistent with the listed five-member example. That last check does not show failure of recovery at higher dimension.
residual_risks: The invariant set is an inner subset of the recovery basin, with strict product condition, not its exact boundary. The convergence claim is continuous-time and not inferred from the numerical trajectory samples.

originality.rationale: The same open model, equilibrium equation and small-cycle local stability are already known. The decisive verified comparison is the 2025 original paper: it proves local upper-equilibrium stability but describes the basin split as numerically motivated and analytically unproved, and its global extinction result concerns the regime without two positive equilibria. The normalized hypercycle theorem does not bound open total mass. No checked source gives the stated sufficient inner basin with an optimal uniform product threshold under the cap. The 2012 comparison was not readable in the independent retrievals; the pass is bounded by the verified material, not an assertion that the historical paper has no overlapping results.
residual_risks: The 2012 historical comparison is a genuine access limitation. The accessible citing passage does not exclude an overlapping positive-equilibrium result elsewhere in that paper.
The searches do not certify publication priority or absence from other historical literature.

value.rationale: The open system has competing extinction and positive equilibria, so local stability and normalized coexistence do not answer whether a given positive initial condition recovers. The theorem supplies a directly checkable, full-dimensional sufficient region, quantitative coordinate lower bounds and an obstruction to uniformly improving the threshold within the proposed class. It is an informative inner basin theorem without claiming to solve the full separatrix problem.
residual_risks: Value concerns this deterministic mathematical model with equal dissipation and the stated small cycle lengths; no empirical, heterogeneous-system or higher-cycle guarantee follows.
